deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study the space of relative positions of one pseudoline D with respect to a fixed arrangement of pseudolines in the real projective plane. 'p.r.' most likely abbreviates 'positions relatives'. The plane is drawn as a disc with antipodal boundary identification. A position is 'stable' when D is in general position (it avoids every vertex of the arrangement). It is 'semi-stable' or a 'specialization' when D passes through exactly one vertex.

The object Δ_D. To each stable position D Grothendieck attaches a combinatorial complex Δ_D. Its 'arcs de transition' record the degenerations or moves available from D. On this page he notes that for a stable D every transition arc of Δ_D is a specialization arc, i.e. D degenerating onto a vertex.

Problem posed. Let D and D' be stable positions obtained from one another by 'balayage': sweeping D across one vertex of the arrangement. This is the elementary triangle-flip or mutation through the intermediate semi-stable position in which D contains the vertex. How do Δ_D and Δ_D' compare? Can one perform a 'surgery' that glues them along the arcs coming from the common specialization?
- He observes there is no ambiguity about which arcs are to be identified.
- He finds it tempting to replace Δ_D and Δ_D' by modified complexes Δ*_D and Δ*_D'. These are obtained by sweeping the boundary (D itself) up to the 'critical' points of interest, and the modified complexes are then glued.

Local model (figures).
- Left figure: D (yellow) and D' (green) lie on either side of a pencil of orange lines through a vertex. This is the balayage over a vertex.
- Right figures: two red pseudolines are drawn in the disc model; their crossing is the vertex. The yellow and green curves (D, D') pass on either side of the two crossing regions shown (top and bottom, which correspond under the antipodal map).
- Marked boundary arcs a, a' (one end) and b, b' (other end) are the local 'stars' (étoiles) where gluing can occur.

Counting. Starting from the symmetric configuration around the intermediate semi-stable position, he enumerates gluings:
- 4 choices of a pair (α, β) in {a, a'} × {b, b'};
- times 2 orientations for gluing α to β;
- giving 8 possibilities.
The crossed pairs (a, b') and (b, a') are excluded by a symmetry or compatibility argument; the reason is partly illegible. That leaves (a, b) and (a', b'), each with two orientations. Modulo the antipodal transformation, which exchanges the primed and unprimed stars, one reduces to the single pair (a, b) with its two orientations.

Purpose. The page belongs to an attempt to understand the global cell structure and homotopy type of the space of stable and semi-stable positions of an added pseudoline. Concretely: how the local complexes attached to adjacent chambers are glued across walls corresponding to sweeping over a vertex. The previous page checks 'circuits' around superposition positions (types A1, A2, B2).
errors: The exclusion of the crossed pairs (a, b') and (b, a') is asserted with a reason that is only partly legible ('à cause de la ... symétrie'). No proof is given on the page and it cannot be verified from the sketch alone.

The reduction by the antipodal transformation assumes the configuration is antipodally symmetric, which the figure suggests. Whether this symmetry is compatible with the chosen gluing orientations is not checked on the page.
The count 8 = 4 × 2 is correct as stated. The whole surgery construction is left unfinished: Δ* is not defined precisely and the outcome of the gluing is not computed.

ideas.what: Moving a pseudoline across a vertex of an arrangement (balayage) as an elementary move between stable positions, through a semi-stable intermediate position
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flip / mutation (Ringel move); sweeping a pseudoline across an arrangement
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Ringel (1956) for mutations and connectivity; Goodman–Pollack (early 1980s) for sweeps and allowable sequences; Edelsbrunner–Guibas (topological sweep, 1986)
ideas.where_published: Only in the unpublished archive notes (cote 154)

ideas.what: Attaching to each stable position of an added pseudoline a local complex Δ_D, whose transition arcs are specializations (D through a vertex), in order to describe the stratified space of positions
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of the space of single-element extensions; extension space / extension poset of an oriented matroid (rank 3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sturmfels–Ziegler, 'Extension spaces of oriented matroids' (1993); Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978); Mnëv–Ziegler
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; pseudoline work is mentioned only allusively in Récoltes et Semailles (unsure of details)

ideas.what: Surgery: gluing the complexes of two adjacent chambers along specialization arcs after 'sweeping the boundary to the critical points' (Δ*), with an enumeration of gluing data (stars × orientations) reduced by mirror and antipodal symmetry
ideas.modern_name: Wall-crossing / gluing of local cell complexes across codimension-one strata; flip-graph and cellular-string arguments
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart known; loosely related to cellular strings and higher Bruhat orders (Manin–Schechtman 1989; Billera–Sturmfels fiber polytopes 1992)

missed.claim: A program to compute the topology of the space of positions of an added pseudoline by surgery across vertex-sweeps. The local complexes Δ_D of adjacent stable chambers are glued along specialization arcs after a boundary-sweep modification Δ*, with the gluing data classified up to symmetry. The construction is begun but not completed.
missed.quote: Ici, il est très tentant de remplacer Δ_D, Δ_D' par Δ*_D, Δ*_D' déduits en balayant le bord jusqu'aux points "critiques" qui nous intéressent, de recoller.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The homotopy type of extension spaces of oriented matroids was the subject of the extension space conjecture, which Liu (around 2020) refuted for realizable oriented matroids in higher rank. As far as I know, the rank-3 (pseudoline) case behaves well. A local wall-crossing or surgery description from 1983–84, independent of Sturmfels–Ziegler, is of historical interest. It might also suggest an explicit inductive proof technique in rank 3, though the page is too fragmentary to assess.

missed.claim: Implicit link between sweeping/flip moves (combinatorial geometry) and a surgery-theoretic, stratified-space viewpoint on configuration spaces of pseudolines. This anticipates themes later developed as realization and extension spaces and as cellular strings / higher Bruhat orders.
missed.quote: Comment se comparent [?] Δ_D et Δ_D', quand D, D' sont déduits l'un de l'autre par balayage au-dessus d'un sommet ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck independently approached oriented-matroid extension topology before the standard references. This is mainly of historical rather than mathematical novelty.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is an exploratory fragment with a small case enumeration (8 gluings reduced by symmetry to one pair). Its interest is that it shows Grothendieck in 1983–84 independently attacking what is now the topology of single-element extension spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids, via a wall-crossing 'surgery' idea. No finished result is legible, and the elementary moves themselves are classical (Ringel, Goodman–Pollack).
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'p.v.' is more likely 'p.r.' (positions relatives); 'surgery' is plausibly correct (Grothendieck uses the English word) but uncertain.
Line 5: 'Comment se rendre' is more plausibly 'Comment se comparent' (Δ_D et Δ_D').

Middle column: roughly '... il n'y a pas d'ambiguïté possible sur les arcs le long desquels faire le recollement, ni par l'intermédiaire de quels arcs de spécialisation ... (il faudrait du coin pour l'intérieur pour recoller !)'. The phrase 'on peut l'anticiper' is doubtful.

Final line on the right reads approximately: 'Mais modulo transformation, par antipodisme du plan et dans D (qui ... la disposition des 2 étoiles) ... (a,b)'. The struck-out word 'applicat[ion]' precedes 'transformation'.
Before 'symétrie' the legible words are roughly 'à cause de la ... [symétrie?]'; the reason for excluding (a,b') and (b,a') is not securely readable.
The star labels in the right figure include b*, b', b̃ (or 'k') near the boundary arcs, not only a, a', b, b'.
